purpose: MSRV hex encoder correctness, not performance comparison

manifest.barrier_clock: CLOCK_MONOTONIC across children in the same Linux time namespace; Unix time is display only
manifest.capacity_guard: planned writer byte credits include payload/records/checkpoint/failed partials/recovery; hard per-file RLIMIT_FSIZE; before-write resource-log cap; whole-tree watchdog at <=1s. No filesystem project quota: unexpected output may exceed the observed aggregate threshold before termination, and actual excess is reported

filesystem.limits: mountinfo identifies this namespace only; ext4 name alone does not verify physical device or MiniPC

manifest.limits: Synthetic owned-buffer FIFO, no SDK/USB/ROS or status-persistence background load. Single/three writer groups share the output filesystem; observer-selected camera count is irrelevant. Process CPU includes synthetic generation/hash and extra readers; VmHWM includes the whole child. Simultaneous group RSS is sampled, not a sum of individual peaks. /proc PID IO includes that process and its threads but page-cache/writeback attribution is incomplete; diskstats are whole-device. No cache dropping, filesystem tuning, queue increase or durability weakening. SIGKILL after a durable checkpoint tests process-crash recovery, not physical power loss. Alternation/repeats improve reproducibility, not statistical significance or proof of unique cause. Overlay/tmpfs/container results do not establish MiniPC/ext4 behavior. Before/after writer-only differences cannot establish capture-service status-path performance.

summary.limits: Synthetic owned-buffer FIFO, no SDK/USB/ROS or status-persistence background load. No cache dropping, filesystem tuning, queue increase or durability weakening. SIGKILL after a durable checkpoint tests process-crash recovery, not physical power loss. Alternation/repeats improve reproducibility, not statistical significance or proof of unique cause. Overlay/tmpfs/container results do not establish MiniPC/ext4 behavior. after.limits: independent process-crash test; not an arbitrary kill point or physical power cut
